title: Revealing the RNA foundations of chromatin-based epigenetics
text:
Epigenetic processes provide a layer of regulation that is above the genetic sequence and are essential to
understand health and disease. In model organisms, such as yeast and flies, noncoding RNAs play important
role in regulating the flow of epigenetic information, but their contribution to these processes in mammals
remains poorly understood at a mechanistic level. We will leverage our expertise in RNA biochemistry,
functional genomics, and mass spectrometry to identify and characterize RNAs that shape transitions in
epigenetic states that accompany the differentiation from embryonic stem cells to neurons.

title: Targeting Intrinsic and Extrinsic Barriers to Treat Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer
text:
Metastatic pancreatic cancer has no effective treatments largely due to tumor cell intrinsic and extrinsic
mechanisms that result in therapy resistance. This proposal will investigate a preclinical treatment strategy that
specifically targets the intrinsic component, namely the ability of pancreas cancer to metastasize, along with the
exquisitely immunosuppressive extrinsic tumor microenvironment. This innovative therapeutic strategy has
never been tested before in PDAC and could open a new avenue of research for a malignancy in dire need of
effective treatments.

title: Identifying stigmatizing language in hospital birthing care: The ID-STIGMA study
text: Variations in perinatal care quality and outcomes persist in the United States, yet no studies have identified how clinical documentation patterns may influence pregnancy care for women and newborns. The proposed study will use natural language processing, a data science approach, to identify documentation patterns and to examine whether these patterns are associated with perinatal morbidity outcomes for pregnant women and newborns. This work will inform the development of clinical decision support, the education and training of clinicians, and the realignment of institutional policies to positively influence documentation quality and optimize patient care.

title: Export and Integration of Ophthalmic Optical Coherence Tomography Data Across Institutions (OCT)
text:
This project will unlock the vast potential of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) imaging data, currently trapped
in incompatible proprietary formats, by developing a uniﬁed open standard and high-performance conversion
tools. We will create turnkey repository software that enables automated extraction from Picture Archiving and
Communication Systems (PACS), seamless integration into clinical IT, and researcher-friendly access for machine
learning and clinical studies. Starting with 17 U.S. institutions and designed for nationwide adoption, this work
will transform OCT data into a shared resource ready for AI applications, accelerating discovery and improving
care for blinding eye diseases.

title: Training Program in Imaging Sciences in Translational Cardiovascular Research
text: Imaging in the biomedical sciences – from the individual molecule to the entire body – is a critical component of research which drives some of the most important discoveries of our time. The development of imaging technologies by scientists should be informed by a knowledge of the important targets around which to develop an imaging strategy, and conversely, biomedical researchers should be fluent in the broad range of imaging platforms available to optimally design their studies – a reciprocal relationship that will foster the kind of scientific discovery that can be translated to the bedside. This Training Program aims to train postdoctoral fellows to acquire core competency in imaging technologies across a broad spectrum, to achieve fundamental proficiency in tools for translational research spanning basic to clinical investigation, and to use these tools to pursue hypothesis-driven research, with a focus on cardiovascular medicine.

title: Novel Role for Host Immunostimulatory RNA in Antiviral Immune Defense
text:
Innate immune sensing and signaling are important first steps of the immune system to initiate
an antiviral response. This study will provide new molecular insight into the host defense
mechanisms against herpesvirus infection, which may catalyze the design of novel therapeutic
approaches for viral diseases.

title: Core E:  Viral Pathogenesis & Persistence
text:
. 
Core E offers a wide suite of modern virology technologies, including viral, cell, microscopy, and sequencing services, to assist new, junior, and established CFAR investigators in obtaining critical data for their projects. The Core has a successful history of providing technologies developed by individual CFAR laboratories and making them available to the broadest possible user base.

title: The CRISPR Vision Program: Nonviral Genome Editing Platforms to Treat Inherited Retinal Channelopathies
text:
Genome editors make targeted changes in the genome and hold great promise in translational research but
moving them into investigational new drugs has been slow and challenging. The majority of products in
development target the liver or utilize viral vectors. Because these strategies are limiting for many diseases,
especially those that affect post-mitotic cells in complex tissues like the eye, the CRISPR Vision Program seeks
to develop novel human genome editing therapeutic platforms for transient, localized, and nonviral treatment of
multiple inherited retinal disorders, specifically channelopathies affecting the retinal pigment epithelium.

title: Episodic Memories of 9/11 terror attack and Mental Health: Natural Language Processing of Adolescent and Adult Survivors' narratives (EMLAS study)
text:
While the long-term mental health effects of the 9/11 attacks on adults are well-documented, less is known
about the impact on children and adolescents exposed to this trauma. Childhood trauma can disrupt the
development of cognitive functioning, emotional regulation, and memory processing, leading to long-term
effects that may emerge years later and be reflected in how the event is recalled. This research aims to use
advanced technology to analyze how survivors' traumatic memories, especially those who were adolescents
at the time, relate to their current mental health, with the aim to guide future mental health interventions.

title: Regulation of Intracellular Signaling
text:
Intracellular signaling is critical to many physiological processes, including cell proliferation, growth,
development, motility, and stress responses. Also, altered signaling is associated with various diseases. The
proposed studies will significantly advance our understanding of the mechanism of intracellular signal
transduction and promote the development of therapeutic interventions for human disorders.

title: Cellular Pathophysiology of Neuronal Na/K-ATPase Dysfunction
text:
The overall goal of this project is to determine the cellular mechanisms responsible for
neurodevelopmental disorders associated with mutations in the gene, ATP1A3. This
gene encodes a protein involved with maintaining ion gradients in neurons, which are
required for normal neuron function. ATP1A3 mutations cause severe childhood-onset
neurological diseases with inadequate treatment options, and our work will help inform
new therapeutic strategies.

title: Regulation of eDHFR-tagged proteins with trimethoprim PROTACs
text:
There is a need for developing small molecule tools that can both control protein function and be used for imaging
in intact animals or patients. Our approach is to genetically alter cells to produce proteins of interest, such as
chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), fused to a small bacterial enzyme called E. coli dihydrofolate reductase
(eDHFR). eDHFR binds very tightly to the clinically-used antibiotic trimethoprim (TMP) and eDHFR-expressing
cells will take up and bind TMP. We have engineered two derivatives of TMP. The first is coupled to a radioactive
isotope that allows quantitative imaging of eDHFR and eDHFR expressing cells in animals using positron-
emission tomography. The second is the focus of this research project, a version of TMP that is tethered to
another small molecule, pomalidomide (POM). These TMP-POM molecules guide eDHFR-fusion proteins to the
protein degradation machinery (e.g. the proteosome) of the cell causing destruction of the fusion protein. We
will apply these molecules to show their ability to regulate the expression of diverse fusion partner proteins, to
show their mechanism of action, and to improve the therapeutic window of CAR T-cells. This project sets a new
precedent for small protein tags which confer dual in vivo imaging and regulation capabilities.

title: Lysosome-targeting chimeras degrading immune checkpoint proteins to enhance immunoradiotherapy of head and neck cancer
text:
There is an urgent need for more effective strategies to enhance the survival and quality of life of
patients with head and neck cancer (HNC). This study highlights the underexplored application of
innovative lysosomal targeting chimeras (LYTACs) to degrade immune checkpoint proteins
overexpressed in HNC, aiming to synergize with both external and internal radiation to enhance
radioimmunotherapy. Our ultimate objective is to expedite the clinical translation of LYTACs to
improve the treatment outcomes for HNC.

title: Cell-type-specific dysregulation and genetic control of alternative polyadenylation in neurodegeneration
text:
mRNA processing and 3’UTR choice is altered in both Alzheimers’ and Parkinson’s disease (PD) but the
molecular and genetic drivers and consequences of this dysregulation remain unknown. I propose to
repurpose existing single-cell and whole genome sequencing datasets to map altered 3’UTR choice in
neurodegeneration, identify variants regulating 3’UTR choice in neurodegenerative disease, and understand
how downstream consequences of 3’UTR choice affect disease. The proposed research is relevant to the
mission of the NIA and to public health because it improves our knowledge of a fundamental molecular layer
altered in both Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s with the goal of understanding genetic risk for neurodegeneration
and developing therapeutic interventions.

title: Controlled Antigen Delivery for Prophylactic Cancer Vaccination
text:
Carcinomas, solid tumors of epithelial origin, represent up to 90% of all cancer cases in the United States and
present a persistent healthcare challenge. Immunotherapy and chemotherapy are promising treatment
strategies for carcinomas, but they have limited efficacy and are associated with side effects that impact
patient quality of life. This F99/K00 award proposal focuses on developing a peptide-based hydrogel for the
local delivery of chemotherapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors to improve treatment efficacy while avoiding
systemic toxicity and side effects.

title: Training Grant in Cell and Molecular Dermatology
text: This program seeks to train physicians and basic scientists in skin research, with the long-term goal of increasing the number of academic dermatologists and skin-oriented biomedical scientists in the workforce. Our trainees will benefit from our department’s expertise in studying common skin diseases such as psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, aging/photoaging and skin cancer, which have major impacts on public health. We will emphasize both basic and "bench to bedside" translational research, while also prioritizing the professional development of all our trainees.

title: Development of genetically encoded sex hormone biosensors to understand neuroactive steroid signaling dynamics in vivo
text:
The development of real-time sex hormone sensors could catalyze advances across multiple fields of
human health, from personalized medicine and reproductive health to the management of hormone-related
disorders like breast and prostate cancer. By enabling precise monitoring of hormone fluctuations, these tools
hold the potential to enhance the understanding and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, mental health
conditions, and contribute to aging research. This technology promises to pave the way for targeted therapies
and interventions, offering new insights into the intricate role of hormones in human physiology and disease.

title: A novel strategy for the next generation rAAV gene therapy and vaccine vector production
text:
The primary goal of this project is to develop a novel platform for efficient production of large quantities of high-quality
recombinant adenovirus-associated virus (rAAV) vectors that can be used to deliver therapeutics genes, immunotherapeutics,
and vaccines. Currently existing systems are inadequate and ineffective for large-scale production of high-quality rAAV.
We will develop an innovative system that can produce high-quality rAAV in mammalian cells by combining with a
baculovirus-based high-capacity protein expression system. Successful completion of this work will have a significant
impact on both the vaccine and gene therapy fields.

title: Next-generation image-guided endoscopic sinus surgery using novel computer vision techniques
text:
Existing computerized stereotactic image-guided surgery (IGS) systems used in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS)
for chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) have significant weaknesses that may compromise clinical outcomes including:
1) high costs, driving lower usage nationally, especially in socioeconomically disadvantaged groups and
geographic areas, which are associated with worse CRS disease severity, 2) loss of tracking accuracy during
surgery, eroding surgeon trust during the surgical dissection, and 3) disparity between the static computed
tomography (CT) images and the reality of the surgical field, which diverge as the surgery progresses, potentially
compromising the completeness of surgery. Computer vision techniques will be used to create three-dimensional
(3D) reconstructions of the surgical field forming the basis for a novel next-generation navigation system that
performs continuous automated co-registration between the 3D surgical scene and the CT to maintain tracking
accuracy, reflects anatomic changes on the CT images in real-time during ESS, overlays critical anatomy on the
live endoscopic view, and continuously tracks all surgical instruments that are in view. This significant advance
in surgical navigation will improve substantially on existing IGS for ESS to drive enhanced clinical outcomes in
CRS by: 1) dramatically reducing the cost and increasing the availability of surgical navigation to all communities
by harnessing typical video-endoscopic equipment used in ESS and eliminating the need for expensive
conventional IGS hardware, 2) achieving consistent and stable submillimeter tracking accuracy during the course
of ESS to improve surgeon confidence, and 3) enhancing the completeness of surgical dissection through real-
time dynamic CT updates, highlighting of critical anatomy, and continuous surgical instrument tracking.

title: Computational tools for precision genome editing
text:
In this project, we will develop computational software and generate extensive datasets to study CRISPR (also
called genome editing) experiments, which are intended to make precise changes in the DNA of living cells. The
software will allow researchers to understand how DNA differences between people may change how CRISPR
works, the spectrum of potential DNA changes that might result from different CRISPR methods, and compare
how experimental parameters may influence these results. This project will help scientists and clinicians develop
precise tools to change DNA sequences in living cells to treat a range of diseases.
